note: A CLASS SWEEP THAT READS DOWN A FILE MISSES MEMBERS OF ITS OWN CLASS IN THAT FILE. The Rill Task 3 widened the channel network 16x, which stales every anti-vacuity floor calibrated against it. Fix round 1 swept for those floors, raised seven of them, and reported the sweep as exhaustive. It was not: the_bank_sign_is_left_of_downstream_and_mirrors_exactly in domains/terrain/tests/channel_properties.rs asserted checked >= 25 sixty lines BELOW two floors that same commit raised, in the same file, against a stated reference (54 pairs, 22 lines, 76 vertices) that the same commit was replacing with 2770/1117/3887 two screens up. Measured 2770 of 2770 - 110x headroom. The failure mode was sweeping by reading down the files already open, which finds floors near each other and near what you were editing. Grep the ASSERTION SHAPE instead: >= FLOOR and > N and .len() >= against any population derived from channels(). Second and larger lesson from the same round: raising a constant and rewriting its assertion message is not the fix. The prose two lines above the assertion, and the doc block above the test, keep stating the old reference and are what a chronicle author copies. In windows/locale/tests/water_reading.rs a five-row step sweep printed by the test contradicted the doc at EVERY depth, and the sentence prefaced read this before quoting the number anywhere still concluded with the old figure. The durable repair is not better prose: compute the attribution numbers IN the test and print them, so the next network change cannot leave them behind. Four figures moved that way. Third: the sweep did not merely shift level, it CHANGED SHAPE - the fordable peak moved from depth 13 to 14 and the collapse to zero at depth 15 stopped happening, because a 3.54e-5 rad step cannot straddle a 1.9e-4 rad mainstem but straddles a 7.35e-6 rad creek easily. A stale number is sometimes a finding wearing a defect coat.
